levels.low: Hardcoded 'admin'/'admin123' compared with plain ==. No rate limiting. Original honeypot behaviour.
levels.medium: Password moved to env var HONEYSCOPE_ADMIN_PASS (default still 'admin123'). Still no rate limiting — the weak default remains exploitable.
levels.high: Env-var password + 5-attempts-per-minute in-process rate limiter. Flaw: lockout is per-process and per-IP; a restarted server or a different IP bypasses it.
levels.impossible: Constant-time comparison (secrets.compare_digest) + rate limiting. HONEYSCOPE_ADMIN_PASS should be set to a long random secret. Not exploitable with the default guessing approach.

hints.low: What are the most common default credentials used for management panels? Check the project README.
hints.medium: The password might not be in the source anymore — but what is the default value of the environment variable if it is never set?
hints.high: There is now a rate limit — but it only applies to this process and this IP. What happens if you use a different IP address, or if the server restarts?
hints.impossible: Nothing to bypass with the documented payloads. The env-var password must be set to something strong. Compare the constant-time comparison with the plain == in lower levels.
